endpoints.name: Client
endpoints.description: One client by id. Requires the workspace id.

endpoints.name: Clients
endpoints.description: The clients in one workspace. Requires a workspace id. The billing entity projects belong to. NOTE this is the same endpoint as Workspace Clients under a second name -- the two are identical and either will do.

endpoints.name: Workspace Projects
endpoints.description: The projects in one workspace, with name, client, active state, billable flag, the hourly rate, colour, and estimated hours. Requires a workspace id. The rate is what turns tracked time into money. Filter with active, which defaults to returning only live projects and so omits completed work from historical totals.

endpoints.name: Workspace Project
endpoints.description: One project by id. Requires the workspace id.

endpoints.name: Workspace Project Users
endpoints.description: Who is assigned to which project, with each assignment's own hourly rate. Requires a workspace id. THE PER-PERSON RATE OVERRIDES THE PROJECT RATE, so billing a project at its headline rate overstates or understates it wherever these exist.

endpoints.name: Workspace Project Tasks
endpoints.description: The tasks within one project, with name, estimated seconds and active state. Requires the workspace and project ids.

endpoints.name: Workspace Task
endpoints.description: One task by id. Requires the workspace and project ids.

endpoints.name: Time Entry
endpoints.description: One time entry by id. Same negative-duration convention for a running entry.

endpoints.name: Current Time Entry
endpoints.description: The entry the caller is running right now, or nothing if the clock is stopped. A live check rather than data.

endpoints.name: Time Entries
endpoints.description: The time entries of the AUTHENTICATED USER, filtered by a date range. Carries description, project, task, tags, billable flag, start and stop, and DURATION IN SECONDS. Two things: it is the caller's own entries only, so a workspace-wide extract is not possible through this endpoint; and a RUNNING ENTRY HAS A NEGATIVE DURATION -- Toggl encodes the start time as a negative number until the entry stops, so summing without filtering those out corrupts the total.

endpoints.name: Current User
endpoints.description: The account the credentials belong to. One record. Pass with_related_data to have workspaces, clients, projects and tags returned alongside, which saves several requests when bootstrapping.

endpoints.name: Workspaces
endpoints.description: The workspaces the authenticated user belongs to, with name, the default hourly rate and currency, and the rounding settings. Every other endpoint needs a workspace id. As with any time tracker, ROUNDING MEANS RAW ENTRY DURATIONS AND REPORTED TOTALS CAN LEGITIMATELY DIFFER.

endpoints.name: Workspace
endpoints.description: One workspace by id, with its settings.

endpoints.name: All Users
endpoints.description: The users in one workspace, as user records with name and email. Requires a workspace id.

endpoints.name: Workspace Clients
endpoints.description: The clients in one workspace. Identical to Clients; the connector carries the same endpoint under both names.

endpoints.name: Workspace Project Groups
endpoints.description: The group-level project assignments in one workspace. Requires a workspace id.

endpoints.name: Workspace Tasks
endpoints.description: Every task across the workspace rather than per project. Requires a workspace id. The efficient way to inventory tasks without walking projects.

endpoints.name: Workspace Tags
endpoints.description: The tags in one workspace. Requires a workspace id. The free-form dimension on time entries beyond project and task.

endpoints.name: Workspace Users
endpoints.description: The workspace MEMBERSHIP records rather than the users themselves -- carrying each person's role, whether they are active, and their labour cost. Requires a workspace id. The cost field is here and not on the user, so any cost-of-time calculation joins through this table.
